body.statement: Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\) such that \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\) and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). Gate reinsertion makes the returned circuit and its required positive margins algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion.
body.justification: Completeness is useful only if it retains the positive formulas already justified by the anchor algorithm.
body.gap: Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen transport do-calculus formulas through ordinary pruning and clustering, but not through fixed-support selector-image normalization.
body.consumer: Existing systematic-selection analyses obtain the same estimand and can adopt the normalized backend without changing valid reported formulas.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published derivation satisfying the two hypotheses in the proposed statement.  We construct its trace by induction over the finite derivation tree.  Its initial context law at a used context \(s\in H\) is
\[
p_H(V\mid S=s)=\frac{p_H(V,S=s)}{\sum_v p_H(v,s)}.
\]
The denominator is positive because the sum is nonempty and every admissible summand is positive under \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  This is exactly the initialization and selector-normalizer entry in \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\).

For an induction step that substitutes a known forced value, use the token \(\sigma=(s,X,r,x_s)\) at the same labelled gate occurrence.  The known zero-one multiplexer gives the polynomial identity between the old occurrence and \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\), and substitution of \(x_s\) into its children is ordinary evaluation of the same recursive equation.  Thus the selector transition emits the published corrected kernel.

For a published reachable fixing step at \(W\), use \(\varphi=(s,W,D,k)\).  Reachability is the same displayed CADMG condition in \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\).  Its division is by the same conditional margin \(m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}\), so cross-multiplication verifies equality of the emitted and published kernels.  The stated hypothesis that all denominators are supported margins, together with \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), makes this division valid throughout \(O_H(\Theta_H)\).

For marginalization, choose the corresponding sum token and use distributivity to obtain
\[
\sum_Z\prod_{k\in L}K_k.
\]
For a proper-district split, choose the district token; the fixed topological quotient orders exactly the factors of the published district factorization.  Cancellation does not change the represented rational function on the domain where the uncancelled registered factors are positive.  The elimination ledger admits precisely the remaining supported denominators, again positive by \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\).

This completes the induction and produces a finite support-licensed trace.  At every stage, \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) identifies the normalized kernel with the kernel obtained after reinserting the original gates, so the final circuit is algebraically the published circuit on the original expansion.  Since the premise calls the published output an identifying derivation, its terminal equality is the target equality.  Therefore, for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\),
\[
F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta),
\qquad O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H.
\]
The construction never uses a selector value outside \(H\).  It constructs a valid trace, but the definitions do not establish confluence or force the lexicographic schedule to select that trace; this is why the proposed statement is the exact conclusion proved.
